@bitoku: This pull request references [Jira Issue OCPBUGS-79544](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/OCPBUGS-79544), which is invalid: - expected the bug to target the "5.0.0" version, but no target version was set Comment /jira refresh to re-evaluate validity if changes to the Jira bug are made, or edit the title of this pull request to link to a different bug. The bug has been updated to refer to the pull request using the external bug tracker.
In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/origin/pull/31013): >This test runs after all other tests to capture CRI-O's goroutine state on every node, providing visibility into stuck operations after the suite has exercised CRI-O under load. > >The test sends SIGUSR1 to CRI-O on each node, reads the resulting goroutine dump from /tmp/crio-goroutine-stacks-*.log, and fails hard if any goroutine is stuck in an image pull (IO wait > 30 min in docker.(*bodyReader).Read -> net.(*conn).Read). Instructions for interacting with me using PR comments are available [here](https://prow.ci.openshift.org/command-help?repo=openshift%2Forigin). If you have questions or suggestions related to my behavior, please file an issue against the [openshift-eng/jira-lifecycle-plugin](https://github.com/openshift-eng/jira-lifecycle-plugin/issues/new) repository.

> [!NOTE] > ## Reviews paused > > It looks like this branch is under active development. To avoid overwhelming you with review comments due to an influx of new commits, CodeRabbit has automatically paused this review. You can configure this behavior by changing the `reviews.auto_review.auto_pause_after_reviewed_commits` setting. > > Use the following commands to manage reviews: > - `@coderabbitai resume` to resume automatic reviews. > - `@coderabbitai review` to trigger a single review. > > Use the checkboxes below for quick actions: > - [ ] ▶️ Resume reviews > - [ ] 🔍 Trigger review ## Walkthrough Adds a Ginkgo node test and helper that trigger CRI‑O to write goroutine dumps on each cluster node, collect those dumps (handling PrivateTmp), parse them for IO‑wait goroutines >30 minutes that show `net.(*conn).Read` followed by `docker.(*bodyReader).Read`, and fail if dumps are missing or stuck image‑pull goroutines are found. ## Changes |Cohort / File(s)|Summary| |---|---| |**CRI-O Goroutine Dump Test & Parser**
`test/extended/node/crio_goroutinedump.go`|New Ginkgo `[sig-node][Late]` test that enumerates nodes, finds CRI‑O PID, sends `SIGUSR1`, waits for `/tmp/crio-goroutine-stacks-*.log` (handles PrivateTmp via `/proc//root/tmp`), returns sentinel strings on failure, and aggregates per-node results. Adds `findStuckImagePulls(dump string) []string` to split dumps into goroutine blocks, parse `IO wait` minutes, filter `minutes > 30`, and detect blocks where `net.(*conn).Read` appears before `docker.(*bodyReader).Read`.| |**Unit tests for parser**
`test/extended/node/crio_goroutinedump_test.go`|New table-driven Go test `TestFindStuckImagePulls` with multiple goroutine-dump fixtures covering stuck and non-stuck cases (including versioned containers/image stacks, boundary 30m case, missing frames, mixed dumps, and empty dump) asserting expected match counts.| ## Sequence Diagram ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant TestRunner as Test Runner participant Node as Cluster Node participant CRIO as CRI‑O Process participant Parser as Dump Parser TestRunner->>Node: run shell to find CRI‑O PID Node-->>TestRunner: PID or CRIO_NOT_FOUND TestRunner->>CRIO: send SIGUSR1 to PID activate CRIO CRIO->>CRIO: write /tmp/crio-goroutine-stacks-*.log CRIO-->>TestRunner: dump file created (or timeout) deactivate CRIO TestRunner->>Node: fetch newest dump file (via /proc//root/tmp) Node-->>TestRunner: goroutine dump content or DUMP_TIMEOUT TestRunner->>Parser: call findStuckImagePulls(dump) Parser->>Parser: split into goroutine blocks Parser->>Parser: extract IO wait minutes, filter > 30 Parser->>Parser: match stack pattern (net.(*conn).Read -> docker.(*bodyReader).Read) Parser-->>TestRunner: list of stuck goroutines alt stuck goroutines found TestRunner->>TestRunner: fail test and emit dumps else no stuck goroutines TestRunner->>TestRunner: pass end ``` ## Estimated code review effort 🎯 3 (Moderate) | ⏱️ ~25 minutes --- > [!IMPORTANT] > ## Pre-merge checks failed > > Please resolve all errors before merging. Addressing warnings is optional. ### ❌ Failed checks (2 warnings, 1 inconclusive) | Check name | Status | Explanation | Resolution | | :------------------------: | :------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Docstring Coverage | ⚠️ Warning | Docstring coverage is 50.00% which is insufficient. The required threshold is 80.00%. | Write docstrings for the functions missing them to satisfy the coverage threshold. | | Test Structure And Quality | ⚠️ Warning | Test lacks meaningful assertion error messages. While it has single responsibility and appropriate timeouts, assertions at lines 146, 152, and 155-162 use bare framework.ExpectError/ExpectNoError without contextual messages explaining which operations failed or why. | Add descriptive failure messages to all assertions explaining what operation was attempted and what failed, such as 'failed to collect goroutine dumps from node: ' + nodeName for context. | | Ote Binary Stdout Contract | ❓ Inconclusive | Code files for the PR are not materialized in the repository, preventing direct inspection for OTE Binary Stdout Contract violations such as unredirected fmt.Print or klog writes at process level. | Provide access to the actual code files crio_goroutinedump.go and crio_goroutinedump_test.go to verify no fmt.Print/Printf/Println or unredirected klog writes exist at process level outside of test It() blocks. |
✅ Passed checks (7 passed) | Check name | Status | Explanation | | :----------------------------------------------: | :------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | Description Check | ✅ Passed | Check skipped - CodeRabbit’s high-level summary is enabled. | | Stable And Deterministic Test Names | ✅ Passed | The Ginkgo test uses static string literals for test names with no dynamic elements like timestamps, UUIDs, or format specifiers. | | Microshift Test Compatibility | ✅ Passed | The test uses only standard Kubernetes Node API and debug utilities with default namespace, contains no OpenShift-specific APIs, and demonstrates MicroShift awareness by handling PrivateTmp behavior. | | Single Node Openshift (Sno) Test Compatibility | ✅ Passed | Test iterates over all nodes and verifies CRI-O functionality with assertion len(nodes)>0, which passes on SNO without multi-node assumptions. | | Topology-Aware Scheduling Compatibility | ✅ Passed | PR adds only diagnostic test code that collects CRI-O goroutine dumps. No deployment manifests, operators, controllers, or workload scheduling constraints are introduced. | | Ipv6 And Disconnected Network Test Compatibility | ✅ Passed | New Ginkgo test uses cluster-internal APIs for node enumeration and local node operations with no IPv4-specific assumptions, hardcoded IPs, or external connectivity requirements. | | Title check | ✅ Passed | The title accurately describes the main change: adding a [Late] test that collects CRI-O goroutine dumps via SIGUSR1 signal. This matches the core functionality implemented in the changeset. |
✨ Finishing Touches
🧪 Generate unit tests (beta) - [ ] Create PR with unit tests
